metabolism pathways, including those involved in the formation of 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin) and 5-hydroxytryptophan in
the central nervous system. Some patients may beneﬁt from the modulation of these pathways by drugs and supplements. People
with AIDS exhibit impairment of NAD production, which can respond to niacin supplements, and high-dose nicotinic acid is being
used as part of the treatment of cardiovascular diseases (see the Section on Dietary Sources and High Intakes below). Diet-associated
pellagra is still prevalent in some African countries, e.g., refugees in Malawi, and in parts of India and China.
